tools.name: keel_recall
tools.label: Keel Recall
tools.description:
Recall earlier parts of this session, including anything dropped by compaction.
Use it before saying the context is gone.

Pick one per call:
- query: keyword search (regex works), 5 results per page.
- range: [from, to]: entries #from..#to in order, 20 per page.
- expand: [N, ...]: full text of those entries.
- mode: 'touched': files worked on, with entry indices.
- mode: 'sessions': this project's earlier sessions (restarts, /new, forks, handoffs).
- query '#N:path': file content from entry N ('#N:path:full' for all lines).

Add to any of them:
- page: next page of query, range, touched or sessions results.
- scope: 'lineage' (default) reads the current conversation path; 'all' also
  reads edited or retried branches; 'project' makes a query search this
  project's earlier sessions too.
- session: an earlier session's id (from mode:'sessions' or a [session id] hit):
  the call reads that session; its #N are its own.

#N is the number shown in summary refs like (#12) and in recall results.
One result is capped at 50 KB (less on a small context window).

query.description: What to recall, in plain keywords (e.g. 'redis cache decision'). Multi-word queries are ranked by relevance. A regex pattern also works. '#N:path' instead shows a file's content from entry N.

range.description: [from, to]: every entry from #from to #to (inclusive) in order, 20 per page. #N is the number in summary refs like (#12) and in recall results.

expand.description: #N indices to return full content for (from summary refs like (#12) or recall results).

page.description: Page number (1-based) for query, range, touched or sessions results. Default: 1.

scope.description: Default 'lineage' covers the active conversation path. Use 'all' to also reach messages from other branches, such as turns that were edited or retried. 'project' makes a query also search this project's earlier sessions.

mode.description: hybrid (default) = normal recall; touched = files worked on, by path, with entry indices (misses files written by shell commands); sessions = this project's earlier sessions, newest first.

session.description: Id (or its first 4+ characters) of an earlier session from mode:'sessions' or a [session id] hit: the call reads that session instead of this one.

tools.name: keel_pin
tools.label: Keel Pin
tools.description:
Pin a short note that must survive every compaction: a decision and its reason, a constraint, a fact
the rest of the task depends on. Pinned notes are kept verbatim at the top of every summary until
unpinned; everything else in a summary ages out on a long task.

- note: the text to pin, one self-contained line (clipped at 300 chars).
- name: optional, with note: a short name for it (e.g. auth-plan). Pinning a name again replaces
  its note, so keep a plan, a decision or a command current under one name instead of adding notes.
- unpin: the [N] or the name of a note that no longer holds.
- neither: list the pinned notes.

Pin sparingly, what you would need if you lost the conversation; the user pins with /keel-pin.

note.description: Text to pin: one self-contained line, e.g. 'Sessions live in SQLite, not Redis: the deploy host has no Redis.'

name.description: A name for the note (letters, digits, . _ -, up to 40 chars), e.g. 'auth-plan'. A note pinned under a name already pinned replaces it.

unpin.description: The [N] or the name of a pinned note to remove.

tools.name: keel_context
tools.label: Keel Context
tools.description:
Decide what stays in your context. Old turns can leave it whole: nothing is summarized or rewritten,
the session keeps every word, and keel_recall expand:[N] reads any entry back exactly. A turn starts at
a user request and holds every call and result after it; the turn running now always stays. Each
request in your context starts with its turn's #N, as [#12], so you can drop by it without listing first.
Your context is also mirrored in a file (its path is the first line of your context): edit it with your
tools, deleting a turn's block, rewriting its text as what to keep, or writing notes between blocks, and the
next request sends what it says. This tool is the short way to the same edits.

- no params: list the turns in context, by #N range and size, and what is out.
- drop: #N refs or ranges ('#12-#40'); every turn they touch leaves from the next request.
- oldest: how many of the oldest turns in context leave.
- restore: #N refs or ranges of turns to bring back.
- note: with drop or oldest, one line kept where the turns were (what they settled, what to look up).
- undo: true reverses the last edit (what it took out comes back, or what it brought back leaves).

Drop rarely and in large runs from the oldest end: each edit makes the provider read again all that
follows it, so a drop that frees too little for that is held back, with the run that would pay (force: true
takes it out anyway: when the user asked for it, or what it holds is done with);
past 85% of where the host compacts, the oldest turns leave by themselves; the user evicts with /keel-evict.

drop.description: #N refs or ranges of turns to take out, e.g. ['#12-#40'] or [12].

oldest.description: How many of the oldest turns in context to take out.

restore.description: #N refs or ranges of turns to bring back into context.

note.description: One line kept in place of the turns taken out (clipped at 300 chars).

undo.description: true: reverse the last edit of the context.

force.description: true, with drop or oldest: take them out even where it does not pay back what the provider reads again.

commands.description: Compact the conversation into a keel structured summary (keep:N keeps the last N user turns)

Recall earlier parts of this session. Plain keywords work best; scope:all reaches edited or retried turns, scope:project this project's earlier sessions; 'sessions' lists them, session:<id> reads one.
Pin a note that stays at the top of every keel summary; name:NAME first names it, and a name pinned again is replaced. No text lists the pinned notes.
Unpin a keel note by its [N] or its name.
Take old turns out of the context whole (no text: the oldest half; N, all, #A-#B, restore #A-#B, list).
